title: Vegan Tuna from Watermelon: Marinaded Watermelon Planks Baked as a Tuna Substitute
summary: In this Goodful episode from the Vegan Substitute series, Merle invites Mae to tackle a viral idea: turning a watermelon into a tuna substitute. They name the watermelon “Victor,” trim and skin it, and cut four planks to marinate. The marinade combines rice wine vinegar, low-sodium soy sauce (or tamari), sesame oil, neutral oil, red pepper flakes, and crumbled nori to impart a fishy flavor. The planks are vacuum-sealed and refrigerated for six hours or overnight, then dried and baked on parchment at a low oven (300°F / 150°C) for 90 minutes. After cooling, the slices are plated on sushi rice and taste-tested by Merle and Mae. The hosts discuss texture, flavor, and the substitution’s viability, noting that while it resembles tuna in appearance and mouthfeel, the flavor remains distinctly watermelon. The video frames the experiment as a playful, competitive cooking challenge within the series, and touches on sustainability practices like composting towels and reusing bags.
